The sources disagree on the date and none gives one start. Sardegna Turismo (Regione Sardegna, sardegnaturismo.it/it/esplora/predio-canopoli) says the dating of the temple is uncertain: for some the Middle Bronze Age (XVI-XIV secolo a.C.), others suggest a later date, between the Recent and Final Bronze Age (XIII-IX a.C.). Italian Wikipedia says only 'Risalente al periodo del Bronzo finale', and a local tourist site says Middle Bronze Age. These fall in different buckets (3000-1500 BC against 1500-500 BC), so the stored -3000 (a band edge, older than even the earliest proposal) is not confirmed and no start can be chosen. Italian period words cannot be recorded as a period name in this lane, and the Megalithic Portal page was not opened.

English, Greek, German and Spanish Wikipedia and ToposText (Hellenistic to Late Antique polis) date Elyros only by its flourishing from the 5th century BC and later events (3rd century BC war with Kydonia, 183 BCE treaty, Roman and Byzantine phases); 'flourishing at least as early as' the Classical period is a lower bound, not a start, and the site is unexcavated per English Wikipedia. The Megalithic Portal and geotour.gr answered 403 to both my fetches, so I could not read them; the Chania Holidays page also says only 'flourishing from the 5th century BC'. No readable source dates the start, so the stored -1500 stays unsourced.

No source dates the start of Earl Shilton as a settlement. Wikipedia, GENUKI and the Hinckley Times give only the Roman pottery industry (early second century AD, the 'first industry' and 'first pottery factory'), a 2000 BC cinerary urn found in a sand pit (a stray find, not the town), and the Domesday Book of 1086 as its first written record, which is a first mention and not a foundation; the Corieltauvi after 100 BC are a regional tribe. The stored -500 is a band edge with no source.

No reputable source dates the start of Inca Uyo. The English Wikipedia article says only that the site was 'important in pre-Inca times'; Spanish Wikipedia calls it a Lupaca site with Inca elements added in 1993; Portuguese Wikipedia says it was still under construction when the Spaniards arrived; tourism pages put its construction in pre-Inca times (machupicchuwayna.com) or in the Inca period (travelandes.com, citing the Tschopiks' 'Inca style'). These accounts disagree and none gives a year, century or reliable period for its start.

The Media Lampung article calls Tebing Tinggi a prehistoric Pasemah megalithic site without any year, century or period for this site; Indonesian Wikipedia's Megalit Besemah article treats the Pasemah tradition as a whole. No page dates this site itself.

The English article says 'The purpose, use, and age of the arrangement are not known' and that 'the precise age of the arrangement remains unknown'; the 11,000-year figure is only a suggestion extrapolated from carbon dating at nearby sites ('could be as old as'), which the same source rejects as an age of this site. No other source found dates the construction of Wurdi Youang, so there is no start to give. Not a Neolithic monument: that period came from a type rule only.

The Whetstones circle (Church Stoke, Powys) was destroyed around 1860-1870 and was never excavated or dated. Wikipedia gives only the span of the stone-circle tradition in general (3300 to 900 BCE) and the Megalithic Portal and Megalithix pages carry no date; no heritage register record or excavation report for this circle was found. A class-wide period (some pages call the Corndon circles Bronze Age, others Neolithic) dates no start for this site.

English Wikipedia on Trink Hill (Nancledra, Cornwall) says only that a round barrow exists at the summit, with no date; the Wikidata item and the Commons category carry no period. The Megalithic Portal and Modern Antiquarian pages returned 403 (Cloudflare) and could not be opened, and the only page that dates the barrow (Grokipedia, 'Bronze Age, circa 2500-800 BCE') is AI-written and excluded; a round barrow's class date is no date for this site. Web search budget was exhausted, so no heritage-record search could be made.

No readable source dates these standing stones: English Wikipedia, stone-circles.org.uk and the Northern Antiquarian describe them as prehistoric or a possible Bronze Age ring only by 19th-century assumption (Knox 1855), with no excavation or dating; the Megalithic Portal and Modern Antiquarian pages returned 403.

English Wikipedia calls Codford Circle a Neolithic hill top enclosure or possible hillfort in its lead but states in the body that there is no archaeological evidence for occupation and that it is an enclosure of unknown but ancient date, so it contradicts itself. Descriptions found by search (an Iron Age excavation write-up in UCL's PAST 53, the Atlas of Hillforts record, Historic England) point to a late Bronze Age to Iron Age date instead of Neolithic, but the UCL page returned HTTP 502 and the Atlas page refused the connection on repeated tries, and the Historic England and Megalithic Portal pages refuse automated requests, so I could not open and quote any of them; a page I could not open is not a finding. No quotable source dates the start.
